name: City Council Meeting
minutes_text:
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Agency,
  Community Development Financing Authority,
  Public Improvement Corporation,
  and Library Board of Trustees*

  October 5, 2009

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Agency, the Community
Development Financing Authority, the Public Improvement Corporation, and the Library Board
of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Ury at 5:02
p.m., on October 5, 2009 at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on September 30, 2009, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the
Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Kelley
  Council Member Ledesma
  Council Member Schlicht (arrived at 5:06 p.m.)
  Mayor Pro Tem MacLean
  Mayor Ury

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  Irwin B. Bornstein, Assistant City Manager/Director of Admin. Services
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Pro Tem MacLean

INVOCATION: Mayor Ury

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Gail Reavis, M.V.: speaking as the City’s representative on the Orange County Vector Control

City Council Minutes  1  October 5, 2009
 Board, she alerted the Council Members to the proposal to privatize some or the vector control
functions such as rat and insect control. Mrs. Reavis stated that she enjoys serving on the Vector
Board and hopes to continue her service however; she would like the Council’s input before she
votes on this proposal as it could have a negative effect on the City of Mission Viejo.

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Conference with City Attorney Concerning One matter of Existing Litigation
  Pursuant to Government Code Section 54956.9(a). The Litigation is City of Mission
  Viejo v. Saddleback Valley Unified School District (SVUSD), Case No. 00300610.

CS2. Labor Negotiations -- The Council Will Provide Direction to its Labor Negotiator
  Pursuant to Government Code Section 54957.6. The Parties to the Negotiations Are
  the City and City's Unrepresented Employees. The City's Negotiator is Dennis
  Wilberg.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:09 p.m., Mayor Ury recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City Council
reconvened at 6:00 p.m. with all five Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that there was no reportable action from Closed Session.

PRESENTATIONS

P1.  Introduction of newly appointed Fire Chief Keith Richter of the Orange County
  Fire Authority and Proclaim October 3 through October 10, 2009 to be Fire
  Prevention Week

  Mayor Ury introduced Fire Chief Keith Richter and presented the Chief with the Fire
  Prevention Week Proclamation.

P2.  Community of Character Award

  Mayor Ury and Crime Prevention Specialist Tammy Descoteaux presented the
  Community of Character Award to Cathy Pilliod of Franchise Services Incorporated (Pip
  and Sir Speedy Printing.)

P3.  Recognize the Mission Viejo Girls Softball 10 & Under District All Star Team

City Council Minutes  2  October 5, 2009
   "Synergy" for Placing 10th at the 2009 Western National Championships

  Mayor Ury presented Certificates of Recognition to the team members and coaches.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Robert Reidel, M.V.: expressed concern with Capistrano Unified School District’s proposal to
change from "at large" to "trustee area only" elections. He stated that the City of Mission Viejo
won’t be well-represented if boundaries are changed and he asked the City Council to hold a
public forum to discuss this matter.

Joanne Reid, M.V.: stated that there is a fire hazard with overgrown brush in the canyon next to
Casta del Sol and the Atria del Sol facilities. She appealed to the City Council to negotiate with
Goldman-Sax to turn the canyon property over so the City can clear the brush for safety.

Debbie Carver, M.V.: representing the Assistance League of Capistrano Valley, she outlined
their services to the community. Ms. Carver announced that Operation School Bell is the
Assistance League’s main philanthropic program and provides clothing for children in need,
including 163 from Mission Viejo last year.

Anna T. Boyce, M.V.: requested the installation of exercise stations around the Village Green at
the Norman P. Murray Community Center.

Jim Samuelson, M.V.: stated that he has a high regard for everyone on the City Council and he
has a great deal of respect for Lance MacLean. He suggested that the Council vote no on the
agenda item for certification of the recall and he encouraged residents to vote no if there is a
recall election.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 2 and 7 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate discussion.

Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem MacLean, seconded by Council Member Ledesma, to approve
the Consent Calendar as described below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

City Council Minutes  3  October 5, 2009
 1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said
  titles which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title
  and further reading waived.

3.  Summary of FY 2009-10 Budget Amendments To Date

  Received and filed.

4.  Check Register dated September 11, 2009, in the amount of $627,762.08

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

5.  Check Register dated September 18, 2009, in the amount of $809,320.79

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

6.  Olympiad Road Pavement Resurfacing, Alicia Parkway to Jeronimo Road (CIP
  202)

  (1) Certified the completion of and accepted the improvements for the subject project; (2)
  authorized the City Manager to sign the Notice of Completion; (3) authorized the City
  Clerk to record the Notice of Completion with the County of Orange and to release the
  faithful performance and payment bonds one year and 35 days, respectively, after the
  date of recordation of the Notice of Completion contingent upon no claims or liens being
  filed with the City; and (4) authorized payment of the final retention 35 days after the
  date of recordation of the Notice of Completion.

PUBLIC HEARINGS

OLD BUSINESS

8.  Mallorca Homeowners Association Slope Maintenance and Ownership

  City Manager Dennis Wilberg presented the staff report and stated that this item is on the
  agenda as a result of the Mallorca Homeowners Association's request to assume
  ownership and/or maintenance of the slope.

  The following expressed opposition to proposal for the City to assume ownership and
  maintenance of the Mallorca slope: Larry Gilbert, M.V.; Neil Lonsinger, M.V.; Joe
  Holtzman, M.V.; and Dale Tyler, M.V.

City Council Minutes  4  October 5, 2009
   The following made comments in favor of the City taking ownership or maintenance
  control of the slope and indicated that the Homeowner Association could provide monies
  towards continued maintenance: Charles Rossi, M.V. and Robert Breton, M.V.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Ledesma, to
  reject the proposal.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

  By consensus, the Council directed staff to let the HOA know of their duties to maintain
  the slope.

9.  Status Update on Construction Activity at 26992 La Paja Lane

  Director of Community Development Chuck Wilson presented the staff report.

  Philip Kohn, Attorney for homeowner, Costa Mesa: provided an updated timeline which
  still indicates a scheduled completion of the project to be December 15, 2009.

  The following spoke in opposition to the ongoing construction at 26992 La Paja Lane and
  outlined continued concerns: Richard Cordova, M.V.; Catherine Jasper, M.V.; Helen
  Stamate, M.V.; and Christine Saracino, M.V.

  The following presented a written statement inquiring about the timeline and a Certificate
  of Occupancy for the residence: Roberto Saracino, M.V.

  Motion made by Mayor Ury, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to direct staff to (1)
  provide the City Council Members with a weekly update which compares the timeline
  presented by the homeowner’s attorney (Mr. Kohn) with the actual progress, and include
  any issues that will prevent the homeowner/contractor from executing on their schedule;
  and (2) return at the next City Council meeting to discuss the possibility of a performance
  bond to be filed by the homeowner.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

City Council Minutes  5  October 5, 2009
 10.  Revised Marguerite Aquatics and Tennis Centers Master Plan

  Director of Recreation and Community Services Kelly Doyle presented the staff report.

  Larry Ryan, Architect with RJM Design Group: presented an outline of the revised
  master plan and answered questions of the City Council Members.

  Director of Recreation and Community Services Kelly Doyle presented the staff report.

  Larry Ryan, Architect with RJM Design Group: presented an outline of the revised
  master plan and answered questions of the City Council Members.

  Larry Gilbert, M.V.: spoke in opposition to the project and stated that the contract should
  not be awarded to RJM Design Group as they monopolize too many of the City’s design
  projects.

  Joyce Saltzgiver, Secretary of the Casta del Sol HOA: stated that the plans for the
  Marguerite Aquatics and Tennis Centers are wonderful and will be a beautiful asset to the
  City however, she objects to the cut-through on Casta Del Sol Drive for exit from the
  parking  lot.

  The following urged the City Council to move forward with the improvements at the
  Marguerite Aquatics and Tennis Centers: Debra Griffith, M.V.; Tom Teichmann, M.V.;
  Wendy Bucknum, M.V.; and Patti Bennett, M.V. Dale Tyler, M.V.: stated that this
  project is not fiscally prudent and he recommended that the City lease the property to the
  members for $1 and let them spend their own funds to upgrade the facility.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem MacLean, seconded by Council Member Kelley,
  approve Master Plan B, which includes the addition of two basketball courts, and move
  forward with the project.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT: None

NEW BUSINESS

STAFF REPORTS

City Clerk’s Report

City Council Minutes  6  October 5, 2009
 16.  Certification of Petition for the Recall of Council Member Lance MacLean

  City Clerk Karen Hamman presented the staff report.

  Matt Corrigan, M.V.: recommended that the City move forward and find resolve to this
  issue rather than talking about where the monies will come from.

  Motion made by Council Member Ledesma, seconded by Council Member Schlicht, to
  (1) receive the City Clerk’s Certification of Sufficiency for the recall petition of Council
  Member Lance MacLean; (2) adopt Resolution 09-45 Amending the Fiscal Year 2009-
  2010 Budget to Pay for Signature Verification Fees for the Recall of Council Member
  Lance MacLean from the unappropriated fund balance of the General Fund; and (3)
  authorize payment of the invoice from the Orange County Registrar of Voters in the
  amount of $43,268.40.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  MacLean
  ABSENT: None

RECESS

At the hour of 8:29 p.m., Mayor Ury declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at 8:36
p.m. with four Council Members present. Council Member Schlicht returned to the dais at 8:38
p.m.

COUNCIL COMMENTS

Mayor Pro Tem MacLean

18.  Mission Viejo Dog Park

  The following spoke in opposition to a Dog Park and/or to the proposed Oso Viejo Park
  location: John C. Connolly, M.V.; Jim Krutcik, M.V.; Joe Holtzman, M.V.; Nora
  Neumiller, M.V.; Ginger Black, M.V.; Dale Tyler, M.V.; Karen Mederes, M.V.; Dave
  Gove, M.V.; Myron Sipp, M.V.; Brian Fitzpatrick, M.V.; and Melora Vandersluis, M.V.
  The following spoke in support of a Mission Viejo Dog Park: Sarah Grimberg, M.V.;
  Linda McGovern, M.V.; Susan Sellers, M.V.; Corissa Sellers, M.V.; Patti McLeod,
  M.V.; Anna T. Boyce, M.V.; Scott Palmer, M.V.; Diane Wiley, M.V.; Sharon Cody,
  M.V.; Eric Daniel Nichols, M.V.; Gordon P. Hite, President of the Casta del Sol Canine
  Companions Club, M.V.; Hailey Buck, M.V.; Cathy Angstadt, M.V.; Ron Ruef, M.V.;
  and Stacey Hopper, M.V.

City Council Minutes  7  October 5, 2009
   The following presented written comments in opposition to a dog park: Gregory Naliboff,
  M.V.; John and Malia Ackerman, M.V.; Samantha Thomas, M.V.; and Matt Corrigan,
  M.V. The following presented written comments in favor of a dog park: Jacki Sellers,
  Aliso Viejo; Nancy Willis, M.V.; Lynne Holley, M.V.; Daniel Wei, M.V.; S. Colby,
  M.V.; Anna Hepler, M.V.; Coleman and Diana Rodgers, M.V.; Robert and Cheryl
  Branson, M.V.; Jason Hall and Danielle Aromando-Hall, M.V.; Nic and Tracy Case,
  M.V.; Irma Kopsfeen, M.V.; Stacey Gledich, M.V.; Douglas Beardsloe, M.V.; Jennifer
  Martin, M.V.; Dr. Matthew Wheaton, DVM, M.V.; and Debbie Corwin, M.V.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem MacLean, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to
  allocate $258,060 plus appropriate professional design service fees to construct a dog
  park (funds will come from the General Fund unappropriated fund balance.)

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT: None

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem MacLean, seconded by Mayor Ury, to direct that the
  dog park be built at the Oso Viejo park, north of the Oso Viejo Community Center and
  adjacent to the Village Green.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, MacLean, and Ury
  NOES:  Ledesma and Schlicht
  ABSENT: None

RECESS

At the hour of 10:10 p.m., Mayor Ury declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at 10:21
p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

2.  City Council Minutes

  Council Member Kelley drew attention to a comment from Council Member Schlicht
  outlined on page 11 of the Minutes. Council Member Kelley clarified that Mission Viejo
  pays for the School Resource Officers within the City's boundaries but we do not pay for
  the Tesoro High School Resource Officer.

City Council Minutes  8  October 5, 2009
   Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem MacLean, to
  approve the minutes for the Regular Meeting of September 21, 2009, as presented.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, Schlicht and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

7.  Highway Safety Improvement Program (HSIP) Grant Application

  Council Member Kelley announced that she removed this item from the Consent
  Calendar to let the public know about something really good that the City is doing. She
  commended Mark Chagnon, Director of Public Works, for his resourcefulness in seeing a
  grant opportunity and applying for it.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem MacLean, to (1)
  adopt Resolution 09-44 Authorizing the Director of Public Works to Submit an
  Application for Highway Safety Improvement Program (HSIP) Grant Funds for
  Emergency Vehicle Preemption (EVP) Systems.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, Schlicht and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, AND COMMITTEE REPORTS

11.  Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Council Member Kelley presented the report.

12.  Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Mayor Pro Tem MacLean presented the report.

13.  San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Council Member Ledesma announced that there has not been a recent meeting of the San
  Joaquin Hills TCA.

City Council Minutes  9  October 5, 2009
 14.  SCAG Transportation & Communications Committee (TCC) Report

  Council Member Kelley stated that she has a report that is not urgent and in the interest
  of time, she will hold it until the next meeting.

STAFF REPORTS (Continued)

City Manager's Report

15.  Request to close the Mission Viejo Library on the dates scheduled for future
  Mission Viejo Readers’ Festivals

  City Manager Dennis Wilberg presented the staff report and Valerie Maginnis, Director
  of Library Services, answered questions of the City Council.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Ury, to approve the
  request to close the Mission Viejo Library on the dates scheduled for future Mission
  Viejo Readers’ Festivals.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT: None

City Attorney's Report

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS (Continued)

17.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as
presented in the staff report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
record.

Council Member Kelley

Council Member Kelley announced that Capistrano Unified School District will conduct a
special election in June to decide whether to elect the Trustees from a specific geographic
location. She expressed concern that this will have negative implications for Mission Viejo so
she will be agendaizing that matter for the next Council Meeting. Council Member Kelley stated

City Council Minutes  10  October 5, 2009
 that this City has lacked representation in the past when our Mello-Roos money was voted on
and spent in other cities and our Measure A monies, which should have been spent in Mission
Viejo, were used outside of the City. She believes it is very important to have Trustees selected
at large and she reiterated that she will place an item on the Agenda for the next meeting.
Council Member Kelley discussed her attendance at the Orange County International Triathlon
where competitors from all over the nation came and appreciated what a great place Mission
Viejo is. She said it was very well received and there were a lot of resident spectators. She also
noted that this event is self-funded and the Triathlon Committee pays for police services so the
City does not incur any costs. Council Member Kelley outlined her attendance at an event
hosted by the Casta del Sol Republican Club with Congressman Gary Miller discussing what is
going on in Washington D.C. and his stance on things such as healthcare. She, Mayor Ury and
Council Member Ledesma also had the opportunity to meet with former Congressman Tom
Campbell yesterday. Mr. Campbell is a candidate for Governor and it was an interesting
opportunity to let him know about the cities concerns with AB 32, SB 375, and the state raid on
city coffers. Council Member Kelley reminded the community that the Walk Against Drugs will
be held on Saturday, October 17, 2009, beginning at 8:00 a.m. at Mission Viejo High School.
After the march there will be an Emergency Preparedness Fair at Oso Viejo Park. She also
announced that she was very proud to learn that Mission Viejo’s Relay for Life won two big
awards at the California Relay for Life Summit in Los Angeles. The Mission Viejo Relay won
the Veteran Event Excellence and the Circle of Excellence from over 350 Relay teams in the
State. Council Member Kelley reminded seniors that the City will host a free flu shot clinic at
the Murray Community Center on November 5, 2009, from 10:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m. and she
announced that the Community of Character word for the month of October is respect.

Council Member Ledesma

Council Member Ledesma drew attention to the Red Ribbon Drug Walk on October 17th and he
stated that he looks forward to scheduling a public discussion with Mayor Pro Tem MacLean.

Council Member Schlicht

Council Member Schlicht informed the Community that the 2nd Annual South County Disaster
Preparedness Expo will be hosted by Pat Bates and will follow the Walk Against Drugs on
October 17th. She also referred to a CDC public notice which reveals that 1/3 of pregnant
women who have suffered from the swine flu have died. Council Member Schlicht stated that
she wishes the City will be pro-active and install hand sanitizers at all public facilities since the
best way for an individual to keep healthy is to keep their hands clean. Council Member Schlicht
asked Irwin Bornstein when the City will file its “Financial Transactions, Consolidated
Statement of Revenues Expenditures and Changes in Fund Balance” report. She noted that the
State requires cities to file the report within 90 days of the end of each fiscal year. Assistant City

City Council Minutes  11  October 5, 2009
 Manager/Director of Administrative Services Irwin Bornstein stated that the report is in process
and for those cities that file on-line, they are allowed a little more time beyond September 30th.
She also asked the City Manager if staff can agendaize an item for Council to discuss the State
issued IOU’s for property tax increments and where the Mission Viejo funds will come from.
City Manger Wilberg stated that staff is planning to bring that matter to the City Council on
November 2, 2009. Council Member Schlicht asked Mayor Ury if he has followed-up on his
idea to let the State take or borrow our housing funds. Mayor Ury noted that that concept is part
of the report that staff is working on.

Mayor Pro Tem MacLean

Mayor Pro Tem MacLean announced that he looks forward to refuting all the lies about him in
the recall and he also looks forward to his public debate with Council Member Ledesma. He
stated that the recall proponents talked about the 13,933 valid signatures yet they don’t talk about
the 3,333 signatures that were insufficient and the 1,124 that were duplicates. He stated that
when you do the math, you’ll find out that 32% of the signatures were not valid. That means the
proponents got 9,538 valid signatures so basically the recall was qualified by 145 signatures, not
the overwhelming 13,933 signatures that they talk about. Mayor Pro Tem MacLean stated that
this recall qualified by lies, exaggerations and half truths which he will make abundantly clear
during the recall campaign and in his public debates. He will figure out a way to have it
moderated and do it in a fair and organized fashion and he looks forward to that opportunity.

Mayor Ury

Mayor Ury offered congratulations to staff on the Readers’ Festival. He stated that he has an
expectation about how well things will go and staff exceeded that wholeheartedly and he was
quite impressed. He stated that he looks forward to seeing everyone at the Walk Against Drugs
at Mission Viejo High School at 8:00 a.m. on October 17th.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 10:49 p.m., there being no further business to come before the City Council at this
session, Mayor Ury adjourned the meeting to Monday, October 19, 2009, at 5:00 p.m.

__________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of October 19, 2009

City Council Minutes  12  October 5, 2009
